items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1958-11-14
items.q: it was both of us that day. He couldn't use his and I used mine.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well, I used B-flat and I had E-flat clarinet in my pocket. Both of them on the parade, right? Yeah, the first E-flat clarinet I used, Landry was working as a sailor for a drum or a war line, and he got it for me as a trial. And I started playing it and Joe, also Joe Watson, not Watkins the drummer, Joe Watson, Watkins, who was playing with the Sam Morgan band. Well they had a band out, I didn't remember which band he was playing. It was the first time he ever used an E-flat clarinet, it was both of us that…
You always did play just Albert's system, I understand.

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-11-01
items.q: Sam, and Stan Brayville, and Joe Watson, I mentioned it, and I'm pretty glad I could Sam.

ctx.x: Would you say you were in demand? Would you say you were in demand? Well, I was, I was a young man.

Because I was younger than more of the fellas. And I could play as much as Dave was playing. Not long, I don't even tell you, knew much as Dave was playing. Like I said, he was a Georgia boy. It wouldn't have played, it was a New York. He was annoyed if that's what he was. Because I didn't care who he was, I was going to play. So, as I didn't care who was playing, I was going to play him. You know? But I knew, I knew things that, what you can do, a fella that's considered better than me, can't do what you can do.…

I go to different places, just to be playing. Now, would you actually sit in with, Braden? I sit in with the old man, Braden's place, oh, I see. So, would there be two parents playing at the same time?

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-10-21
items.q: INTERVIEWER: He taught you to play the... INTERVIEWEE: No, he didn't teach me. He was a client.

ctx.x: When you go and buy a reed, is there any particular make you buy? Yeah, I buy a lavore.

What is that? I lay your reed lavore. Lavore? It's supposed to be French. Well, all the reeds are supposed to be French. Sometimes I get a vibrator. I usually use a... I get a name reed. That ain't important, but I use it. That reed was my foist reed. But I always like the stiff reed. Because of the car, I learned stiff reed by playing funerals before I started on E-flat. In parades it wasn't B-flat chronic. And he's got the blue leg of hell. And then, uh... When I switched into E-flat, Sam Walgans granted us.…

To make sure this recording... Um... We were just talking about, uh... What was his name? Joe... Joe Watson. Joe Watson. He taught you to play the... No, he didn't teach me. He was a client. He didn't teach me. No, but no.
